title: Senior Software Engineer, Build Loop
description: Webflow is the agentic web marketing platform for modern marketing teams, helping organizations build, manage, and optimize high-performing web experiences that drive predictable growth and strengthen brand trust. Building at Webflow will need grit, because we move fast, without ever sacrificing craft or quality. We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help us build the next generation of Agentic Codebases About the role: Location: Remote-first (Argentina) Permanent, full-time employee (this is not a contractor position) Application Information: Application deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis until position is closed and filled This posting is for an existing vacancy Reporting to the Senior Engineering Manager, Developer Productivity As a Senior Software Engineer, Developer Productivity , you'll: Design and build the Nest.js service scaffolding that lets product teams stand up new backend services in our next-generation monorepo Implement paved paths, generators, and the platform primitives that make a new service work on day one rather than after a week of wiring. Build the seams that let new services run independently of our existing monolith. Own the deployment story for services and web applications on Cloudflare, and the interoperability with our existing AWS and Kubernetes estate managed through Pulumi and Argo CD. Lead migrations of substantial codebases into the monorepo and turn each one into a repeatable recipe rather than a bespoke effort. Partner directly with product teams as platform customers, treating their adoption as the measure of success and their friction as your backlog. Raise the leverage of the whole team by encoding what you learn into tooling, generators and agent-assisted workflows, so the next migration costs less than the last. Participate in engineering citizenship activities such as co-authoring engineering blogs, strengthening our hiring processes, and leading internal hackathon teams. About you Requirements: BA/BS Degree or equivalent experience 5+ years building and operating backend services in production Demonstrated experience in backend service design defining service boundaries, contracts and data ownership, not only implementing within them Business-level fluency to read, write and speak in English You'll thrive as a Senior Software Engineer, Developer Productivity, if you: Have worked inside a large, heavily-coupled codebase and found the seams: extracting or bypassing functionality incrementally, behind behaviour-preserving contracts Are fluent in TypeScript and Node, and comfortable with edge runtimes. Have hands-on experience with monorepo tooling at scale (Nx, Turborepo or similar) and understand why build-graph correctness is a product concern rather than a config detail. Treat migration work as engineering rather than chores: you budget for the parts that fail silently, verify generated output rather than trusting a green build, and know that bug-for-bug translation beats improvement when the goal is proving nothing changed. Enjoy being a platform engineer with real customers — partnering with product teams, adapting the platform to how they actually work rather than requiring them to change, and measuring yourself on their adoption. Are comfortable working across cloud boundaries, with a considered view on where a workload belongs and what crossing between clouds costs in latency and spend. Communicate decisions in writing well enough that someone can pick up your work from the ticket — and are willing to say plainly when the fast answer and the right answer diverge. Stay curious and open to growth — demonstrating a proactive embrace of AI, and actively building and applying fluency in emerging technologies to elevate how we work, drive faster outcomes, and expand collective impact. Our Core Behaviors: Build lasting customer trust. We build trust by taking action that puts customer trust first. Win together. We play to win, and we win as one team. Success at Webflow isn't a solo act. Reinvent ourselves. We don't just improve what exists, we imagine what's possible. Own it all the way. We move fast because the moment demands it, and we hold ourselves accountable to deliver outcomes — for each other, and for customers. Benefits Ownership in what you help build. Every permanent Webflower receives equity (RSUs) in our growing, privately held company. Health coverage that actually covers you. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for full-time employees and their dependents, with Webflow covering most premiums. Support for every stage of family life . 12 weeks of paid parental leave for all parents and 6+ weeks of additional paid leave for birthing parents. Plus inclusive care for family planning, menopause, and midlife transitions. Time off that’s actually off. Flexible vacation, paid holidays, and a sabbatical program to help you recharge and come back inspired. Wellness for the whole you. Access to mental health resources, therapy and coaching. Invest in your future. A 401(k) with 100% employer match (up to $6,000/year) in the U.S., and support for retirement savings globally. Monthly stipends that flex with your life. Localized support for work and wellness expenses — from Wi-Fi to workouts. Bonus for building together. All full-time, permanent, non-commission employees are eligible for our annual WIN bonus program. Temporary employees may be eligible for paid holiday and time off, statutory leaves of absence, and company-sponsored medical benefits depending on their Fixed Term Contract and their country/state of employment. Remote, together At Webflow, equality is a core tenet of our culture. We are an Equal Opportunity (EEO)/Veterans/Disabled Employer and are committed to building an inclusive global team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, beliefs, and experiences. Employment decisions are made on the basis of job-related criteria without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other classification protected by applicable law. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Webflow will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Stay connected Not ready to apply, but want to be part of the Webflow community? Consider following our story on our Webflow Blog , LinkedIn , X (Twitter) , and/or Glassdoor . Please note: We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Upon interview scheduling, instructions for confidential accommodation requests will be administered. To join Webflow, you'll need a valid right to work authorization depending on the country of employment. If you are extended an offer, that offer may be contingent upon your successful completion of a background check, which will be conducted in accordance with applicable laws. We may obtain one or more background screening reports about you, solely for employment purposes. For information about how Webflow processes your personal information, please review Webflow’s Applicant Privacy Notice .

  • Have worked inside a large, heavily-coupled codebase and found the seams: extracting or bypassing functionality incrementally, behind behaviour-preserving contracts
  • Are fluent in TypeScript and Node, and comfortable with edge runtimes.
  • Have hands-on experience with monorepo tooling at scale (Nx, Turborepo or similar) and understand why build-graph correctness is a product concern rather than a config detail.
  • Treat migration work as engineering rather than chores: you budget for the parts that fail silently, verify generated output rather than trusting a green build, and know that bug-for-bug translation beats improvement when the goal is proving nothing changed.
  • Enjoy being a platform engineer with real customers — partnering with product teams, adapting the platform to how they actually work rather than requiring them to change, and measuring yourself on their adoption.
  • Are comfortable working across cloud boundaries, with a considered view on where a workload belongs and what crossing between clouds costs in latency and spend.
  • Communicate decisions in writing well enough that someone can pick up your work from the ticket — and are willing to say plainly when the fast answer and the right answer diverge.
  • Stay curious and open to growth — demonstrating a proactive embrace of AI, and actively building and applying fluency in emerging technologies to elevate how we work, drive faster outcomes, and expand collective impact.

Our Core Behaviors:

  • Build lasting customer trust. We build trust by taking action that puts customer trust first.
  • Win together. We play to win, and we win as one team. Success at Webflow isn't a solo act.
  • Reinvent ourselves. We don't just improve what exists, we imagine what's possible.
  • Own it all the way. We move fast because the moment demands it, and we hold ourselves accountable to deliver outcomes — for each other, and for customers.

Benefits

  • Ownership in what you help build. Every permanent Webflower receives equity (RSUs) in our growing, privately held company.
  • Health coverage that actually covers you. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for full-time employees and their dependents, with Webflow covering most premiums.
  • Support for every stage of family life. 12 weeks of paid parental leave for all parents and 6+ weeks of additional paid leave for birthing parents. Plus inclusive care for family planning, menopause, and midlife transitions.
  • Time off that’s actually off. Flexible vacation, paid holidays, and a sabbatical program to help you recharge and come back inspired.
  • Wellness for the whole you. Access to mental health resources, therapy and coaching.
  • Invest in your future. A 401(k) with 100% employer match (up to $6,000/year) in the U.S., and support for retirement savings globally.
  • Monthly stipends that flex with your life. Localized support for work and wellness expenses — from Wi-Fi to workouts.
  • Bonus for building together. All full-time, permanent, non-commission employees are eligible for our annual WIN bonus program.

Temporary employees may be eligible for paid holiday and time off, statutory leaves of absence, and company-sponsored medical benefits depending on their Fixed Term Contract and their country/state of employment.

Remote, together

title: Engineering Manager
description: At NetBox Labs , our mission is to make it easier to build and manage complex networks. As a product company, we do that by developing innovative software for network professionals delivered on-premises and in the cloud. We believe in the power of community and collaboration, and we are looking for a hands-on, player-coach Engineering Manager to lead one of our talented teams. These teams build our core software applications including NetBox and NetBox Add-ons, SDKs, and Plugins, and our observability suite including Diode, Diode Agents and SDKs, and Orb. Much of this development is open source and done in collaboration with our community, but also spans source-available and proprietary software. This role reports to the Director of Engineering. In this role you will: Lead a squad of engineers day-to-day while staying hands-on: reviewing code, jumping into design discussions, and occasionally shipping code yourself to unblock the team or model best practices. Drive execution relentlessly — break down ambiguous problems into clear plans, set sprint goals, remove blockers fast, and hold the team accountable to deadlines. Own the software development lifecycle for your team's projects, from planning and design through implementation, testing, and release. Run effective sprint planning, stand-ups, and retros using GitHub and internal tools, helping engineers break work into well-scoped, executable pieces. Champion modern, secure software development practices and keep quality bars high without slowing the team down. Partner closely with product managers to translate customer and community problems into shippable plans, pushing back with data when scope or timelines don't add up. Coach and mentor engineers individually — give direct, timely feedback, help them grow technically, and build a strong bench for future hiring. Foster a culture of ownership, continuous improvement, and knowledge sharing within the team. Act as a liaison between your team and the broader tech community, supporting open-source contributors and guiding community-facing initiatives where relevant. Report progress transparently to engineering leadership, flagging risks early rather than after they've become problems. Stay close enough to the code and the architecture to make credible calls on technical trade-offs, while trusting your engineers to own the details of implementation. You will work closely with: Director of Engineering to coordinate cross-functional initiatives and ensure your team's work runs smoothly in our commercial products. Product team to understand customer and community problems and turn them into a stellar user experience. Peer engineering managers to plan cross-functional projects, clarify ownership, surface dependencies, and clear blockers together. Qualifications: 2+ years of experience as an Engineering Manager or Team Lead, ideally in a player-coach capacity where you're still writing code or reviewing PRs regularly. A track record of driving projects to completion on tight timelines, with a strong bias toward action and unblocking your team over process for its own sake. Strong technical background sufficient to review designs and code, and earn credibility with senior engineers. Experience with Agile methodologies, DevOps, and CI/CD in a fast-moving environment. Proficiency with GitHub for code management, project tracking, and collaboration. Solid understanding of software security principles and practices. Experience with open-source software development and community engagement is a plus. Excellent, direct communication skills — comfortable giving and receiving fast feedback in a remote, async-first environment. Proven ability to coach engineers and help them grow, while still being the person who rolls up their sleeves when the team needs it. It would be fantastic if you have the following background: Networking industry experience. Familiarity with Python, Django, Go, gRPC, or OpenTelemetry. Knowledge of cloud platforms and services (e.g., AWS, Azure). Familiarity with containerization and orchestration tools (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes). Understanding of data privacy regulations and compliance requirements. About NetBox Labs: NetBox Labs helps companies build and manage complex networks. We help customers accelerate network automation by delivering open, composable products and supporting the network automation community. NetBox Labs is the commercial steward of open source NetBox, the world’s most popular network source of truth, and Orb, the next-generation open source network observability platform. Our products include NetBox Enterprise, a fully supported self-managed NetBox with advanced features, and NetBox Cloud, a secure, scalable, and reliable SaaS edition of NetBox. NetBox powers thousands of companies, and NetBox Labs is backed by investment from Notable Capital (formerly GGV), Grafana Labs CEO Raj Dutt, Flybridge, IBM, Salesforce Ventures, and Mango Capital. Our culture and values: We own and solve problems with high attention to detail. Our open source contributors, users, customers & team are all part of our community. When our community wins, we win. We prioritize simplicity and think twice before adding complexity Clear communication helps keep our team aligned and collaborating smoothly. NetBox Labs is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe diverse teams build better software, and we welcome applicants of every race, color, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, and veteran status. If you need accommodation at any point in the process, just let us know.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Add-Ons
description: Why Mozilla ? Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. About this team and role: addons.mozilla.org (AMO) is the foundation of the Firefox add-ons ecosystem. It’s a showcase for developers to publish and grow their extensions, and a place of discovery for millions of users who customize Firefox to make it their own. Behind the scenes are the DevHub which enables developers to manage their extensions. To manage the ecosystem there are a series of Reviewer tools and automated moderation systems. As a Senior Software Engineer, you’ll bring a passion for crafting resilient systems that accelerate our review and moderation teams to provide a first-class experience for Add-on developers. You’ll work closely with engineers, reviewers, developer support, and Add-ons leadership to turn ideas into polished features, modernize the platform and its architecture, and see your work reach millions of people around the world. What you’ll do: Deliver major features and architectural improvements across the Add-ons stack, including automated moderation pipelines, Reviewer tools, and DevHub. Help establish and maintain engineering standards across areas such as code review, definition of done, production readiness, runbooks, incident response, on-call practices, coding conventions, and infrastructure as code. Create robust observability systems and data-backed insights. Provide peer feedback, share knowledge and help others grow. Build and improve the systems that enable Add-ons engineering to safely develop, deploy, observe, and operate production services. Improve our CI/CD pipelines using declarative, pipeline-as-code approaches that make changes reproducible, testable, and easy to review. Deliver work iteratively using a visible backlog, short feedback cycles, retrospectives, and demonstrations to stakeholders. Write clear technical documentation, including design notes, Architecture Decision Records, runbooks, and incident write-ups. Work effectively in unfamiliar codebases, tracing requests and asynchronous jobs end-to-end to understand failures and identify opportunities for improvement. Collaborate with designers, product managers, QA, and community contributors to deliver end-to-end improvements. Contribute in the open through pull requests, code reviews, and discussions. Work on: Feature development: submission flows, trust and safety signals, DevHub and Reviewer tools modernization. AMO application systems: Work within our Python/Django, MySQL, React/TypeScript, and asynchronous processing systems. Internal developer platforms : Create tools and paved paths that make it easier for teams to ship and operate software safely and consistently. Team Process: Contribute to team ceremonies, execute process improvement, and provide feedback on team effectiveness. Engineering standards : Help make production readiness, testing, recoverability, documentation, and safe deployment part of the normal development lifecycle. Platform reliability: Deployments, monitoring, and incident response. What you’ll bring: Strong hands-on experience building and maintaining production applications with Python/Django. Experience operating and improving production software systems where reliability and safe delivery matter. Strong experience with CI/CD systems and treating pipelines and infrastructure declaratively as code. Experience designing or improving automated testing and deployment workflows, including integration testing and staged or progressive delivery. Strong understanding of observability as an engineering discipline, including metrics, logging, tracing, service-level objectives, and actionable alerting. Experience building or maintaining internal tools or platforms used by other engineering teams, with an understanding that internal systems have users, reliability expectations, roadmaps, and lifecycle considerations. Experience defining or improving engineering practices such as code review standards, operational readiness, runbooks, incident response, on-call expectations, or definitions of done. Ability to read and understand unfamiliar codebases and trace application behavior across frontend, backend, asynchronous jobs, data stores, and infrastructure. Experience debugging complex production issues and turning what you learn into lasting system improvements. Strong technical writing skills, with experience creating useful documentation such as design documents, ADRs, runbooks, and incident reports. Experience working iteratively with a visible backlog, regular stakeholder feedback, and retrospectives that result in concrete improvements. Strong collaboration and communication skills in a distributed team environment. A willingness to share knowledge and mentor peers in operational and reliability practices. Commitment to our values: Welcoming differences Being relationship-minded Practicing responsible participation Having grit Bonus points for: Experience with Google Cloud and operating Kubernetes. Experience with infrastructure-as-code tooling and policy-as-code. Experience establishing SLOs and error-budget-based reliability practices. Experience with chaos engineering, disaster recovery testing, or production readiness reviews. Experience with trust and safety, automated moderation, abuse prevention, or other adversarial systems. Contributions to open source projects What you’ll get: Generous performance-based bonus plans to all eligible employees - we share in our success as one team Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute) Quarterly all-company wellness days where everyone takes a pause together Country specific holidays plus a day off for your birthday One-time home office stipend Annual professional development budget Quarterly well-being stipend Considerable paid parental leave Employee referral bonus program Other benefits (life/AD&D, disability, EAP, etc. - varies by country) About Mozilla Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Join us to work on the Web as the platform and help create more opportunity and innovation for everyone online. Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging Mozilla understands that valuing diverse creative practices and forms of knowledge are crucial to and enrich the company’s core mission. We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, persons of all sexual orientations, gender identities, and expressions. We will ensure that qualified individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, as appropriate. Please contact us at hiringaccommodation@mozilla.com to request accommodation. We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race (including hairstyle and texture), religion (including religious grooming and dress practices), gender, gender identity, gender expression, color, national origin, pregnancy, ancestry, domestic partner status, disability, sexual orientation, age, genetic predisposition, medical condition, marital status, citizenship status, military or veteran status, or any other basis covered by applicable laws. Mozilla will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics or any other unlawful behavior, conduct, or purpose. Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.
The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About this team and role:

addons.mozilla.org (AMO) is the foundation of the Firefox add-ons ecosystem. It’s a showcase for developers to publish and grow their extensions, and a place of discovery for millions of users who customize Firefox to make it their own. Behind the scenes are the DevHub which enables developers to manage their extensions. To manage the ecosystem there are a series of Reviewer tools and automated moderation systems.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you’ll bring a passion for crafting resilient systems that accelerate our review and moderation teams to provide a first-class experience for Add-on developers. You’ll work closely with engineers, reviewers, developer support, and Add-ons leadership to turn ideas into polished features, modernize the platform and its architecture, and see your work reach millions of people around the world.

What you’ll do:

  • Deliver major features and architectural improvements across the Add-ons stack, including automated moderation pipelines, Reviewer tools, and DevHub.
  • Help establish and maintain engineering standards across areas such as code review, definition of done, production readiness, runbooks, incident response, on-call practices, coding conventions, and infrastructure as code.
  • Create robust observability systems and data-backed insights.
  • Provide peer feedback, share knowledge and help others grow.
  • Build and improve the systems that enable Add-ons engineering to safely develop, deploy, observe, and operate production services.
  • Improve our CI/CD pipelines using declarative, pipeline-as-code approaches that make changes reproducible, testable, and easy to review.
  • Deliver work iteratively using a visible backlog, short feedback cycles, retrospectives, and demonstrations to stakeholders.
  • Write clear technical documentation, including design notes, Architecture Decision Records, runbooks, and incident write-ups.
  • Work effectively in unfamiliar codebases, tracing requests and asynchronous jobs end-to-end to understand failures and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Collaborate with designers, product managers, QA, and community contributors to deliver end-to-end improvements.
  • Contribute in the open through pull requests, code reviews, and discussions.
  • Work on:
    • Feature development: submission flows, trust and safety signals, DevHub and Reviewer tools modernization.
    • AMO application systems: Work within our Python/Django, MySQL, React/TypeScript, and asynchronous processing systems.
    • Internal developer platforms: Create tools and paved paths that make it easier for teams to ship and operate software safely and consistently.
    • Team Process: Contribute to team ceremonies, execute process improvement, and provide feedback on team effectiveness.
    • Engineering standards: Help make production readiness, testing, recoverability, documentation, and safe deployment part of the normal development lifecycle.
    • Platform reliability: Deployments, monitoring, and incident response.

What you’ll bring:

  • Strong hands-on experience building and maintaining production applications with Python/Django.
  • Experience operating and improving production software systems where reliability and safe delivery matter.
  • Strong experience with CI/CD systems and treating pipelines and infrastructure declaratively as code.
  • Experience designing or improving automated testing and deployment workflows, including integration testing and staged or progressive delivery.
  • Strong understanding of observability as an engineering discipline, including metrics, logging, tracing, service-level objectives, and actionable alerting.
  • Experience building or maintaining internal tools or platforms used by other engineering teams, with an understanding that internal systems have users, reliability expectations, roadmaps, and lifecycle considerations.
  • Experience defining or improving engineering practices such as code review standards, operational readiness, runbooks, incident response, on-call expectations, or definitions of done.
  • Ability to read and understand unfamiliar codebases and trace application behavior across frontend, backend, asynchronous jobs, data stores, and infrastructure.
  • Experience debugging complex production issues and turning what you learn into lasting system improvements.
  • Strong technical writing skills, with experience creating useful documentation such as design documents, ADRs, runbooks, and incident reports.
  • Experience working iteratively with a visible backlog, regular stakeholder feedback, and retrospectives that result in concrete improvements.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills in a distributed team environment.
  • A willingness to share knowledge and mentor peers in operational and reliability practices.
  • Commitment to our values:
    • Welcoming differences
    • Being relationship-minded
    • Practicing responsible participation
    • Having grit

Bonus points for:

  • Experience with Google Cloud and operating Kubernetes.
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code tooling and policy-as-code.
  • Experience establishing SLOs and error-budget-based reliability practices.
  • Experience with chaos engineering, disaster recovery testing, or production readiness reviews.
  • Experience with trust and safety, automated moderation, abuse prevention, or other adversarial systems.
  • Contributions to open source projects

What you’ll get:

  • Generous performance-based bonus plans to all eligible employees - we share in our success as one team
  • Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute)
  • Quarterly all-company wellness days where everyone takes a pause together
  • Country specific holidays plus a day off for your birthday
  • One-time home office stipend
  • Annual professional development budget
  • Quarterly well-being stipend
  • Considerable paid parental leave
  • Employee referral bonus program
  • Other benefits (life/AD&D, disability, EAP, etc. - varies by country)

About Mozilla

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Join us to work on the Web as the platform and help create more opportunity and innovation for everyone online.

Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging

Mozilla understands that valuing diverse creative practices and forms of knowledge are crucial to and enrich the company’s core mission. We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, persons of all sexual orientations, gender identities, and expressions.

We will ensure that qualified individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, as appropriate. Please contact us at hiringaccommodation@mozilla.com to request accommodation.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race (including hairstyle and texture), religion (including religious grooming and dress practices), gender, gender identity, gender expression, color, national origin, pregnancy, ancestry, domestic partner status, disability, sexual orientation, age, genetic predisposition, medical condition, marital status, citizenship status, military or veteran status, or any other basis covered by applicable laws. Mozilla will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics or any other unlawful behavior, conduct, or purpose.

title: Chief Technology Officer - US-Based
description: About Toptal Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe , Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce . We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold. Position Description: As Chief Technology Officer, you will drive execution for the product and engineering teams and put AI at the core of everything the company builds. You will own Toptal’s full technical architecture and you will build it AI-first—utilizing best practices for agentic engineering. AI is not a workstream inside the engineer team—its core to it. You will create and own the AI architecture and best practices the rest of the company utilizes. You will also own the initiatives that put agents into production. You should know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up, how to engineer best-in-class harnesses, and how to create best practices for agentic engineering that engineering teams adopt to 10x their productivity—without sacrificing quality. Your mindset will be that of a builder and an architect, someone who solves problems in the system itself. No problem will be too large or too small for you to solve yourself. You will set the technical direction and hold the cadenced meetings that turns technical strategy into working, production-ready outcomes. You will be in the design reviews and in the code, not adjacent to them. You will move fast, and you will ensure our engineering team is never the reason an initiative slows down. You are the technical owner of all Toptal’s products. You will collaborate closely with Product to design infrastructure that exposes Toptal’s core business logic through modular interfaces the rest of the business can build on. Alongside a group of hands-on executives, your engineering discipline directly shapes Toptal’s growth, profitability, and operational excellence. You will own resourcing and workforce planning as a doer: scoping the work, sizing the teams, planning headcount against it, defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing it off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about hiring A-players—with a sense of urgency. Then, you lead the team. You will set the standards, develop people against those standards, and know exactly who is meeting those standards. You will be one of Toptal’s foremost experts on AI, and you will stay ahead of a field that never stops moving. You will coach engineers on agentic best practices, show the executive team what is newly possible with the new AI tooling, and push AI into every function at Toptal. This role runs on high-energy execution and attention to detail. You will bring urgency to every part of it and measure yourself on outcomes. We are not looking for someone to oversee this work. We are looking for someone to drive it and get into the details. This is a remote position. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English. Responsibilities: The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills. One precondition runs through all of it: you conceive the strategy. You will form your own view of where engineering and AI should go, build the case, and bring the CEO a strategy to react to, not a request for direction. AI and agentic engineering Own Toptal’s AI technology strategy and the architecture beneath it: model selection and fine-tuning, harness design, orchestration, retrieval, context engineering, tool and MCP integration, guardrails, evaluation, and cost control, exposed as primitives every team composes against. Deploy agentic engineering at scale against the work that runs this business: matching, vetting, onboarding, delivery, and internal operations. Own the outcomes those agents are accountable for. Make AI quality measurable. Own the evals, the regression suites, and the review loops, so quality here is proven rather than claimed. Rebuild how the platform gets built and operated, raising output per engineer through AI-assisted development, review, testing, and operations. Engineers have to want this, not comply with it, and creating that pull is on you. Team, resourcing, and accountability Decide what a team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product. Own resourcing and workforce planning: scope the roadmap into buildable work, plan headcount and sequence, write the specs, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments. Own the bar for the team: assess talent honestly, develop people against the bar, and hold it as the organization grows. Platform and execution Own the architecture end to end, from services and data flows to interfaces and system boundaries, and hold the standards that keep it coherent as it grows. Own throughput, reliability, and the platform layer beneath them, including the AI-dependent paths where latency, drift, and provider outages are real failure modes. Own build-versus-buy, technical debt, secure-by-design architecture, responsible AI, and the engineering and AI cost structure down to inference and token spend. In the first week, expect to: Learn Toptal’s model and platform architecture, and meet the leaders you will depend on across Engineering, Product, Industries, and Services. Establish a direct, working rhythm with the CEO. In the first month, expect to: Assess the engineering function honestly, and assess AI maturity with it: what is really in production, what is measured, what is duplicated, and what should be shut down. Assess the team against the bar this role requires, and bring the executive team a strategy no one asked you for. In the first three months, expect to: Be executing your own plan, with a review cadence and clear accountability at every level, and your resourcing plan presented. Stand up the shared AI architecture and evals, and put one agentic workflow into production with a baseline and a measured result. In the first six months, expect to: Show business impact from agents in production in at least two core workflows, with the evidence behind it. Have the leadership team you need, with the bar visibly raised, and throughput and reliability moving on the paths that matter most. In the first year, expect to: Run an engineering organization recognized inside and outside Toptal as one of the most advanced in the industry, with the pull on AI now coming from engineering. Have AI leverage embedded in the architecture and the operating model, not living in a portfolio of pilots, and the team you built delivering against plan. Qualifications and Job Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field is required, and an advanced degree is strongly preferred. 15+ years of progressive engineering leadership, including significant time as a CTO or VP of Engineering, or as a direct report to one at meaningful scale. Deep, current, hands-on command of modern AI engineering: foundation models, agentic architectures, harness design, retrieval, context engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation. You have shipped and operated these in production, and you know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up. Agentic systems deployed at scale against real business processes, with measured outcomes on cost, cycle time, quality, or revenue, and a record of retiring what did not work. Rigor about evaluation. You can explain precisely how you knew a model, prompt, or agent change was an improvement, and you can show the evidence. Command of the economics underneath it: model routing, hosted versus self-hosted, inference capacity, latency and cost budgets, and staying portable across providers. Further ahead on AI than the executives around you, able to teach it, and proven at moving an organization to adopt something it was not asking for. You create strategy rather than administer it, and you win arguments on evidence rather than authority, including your view on what a team should look like in the age of AI. Proven ownership of resourcing and workforce planning, and a hiring track record you can quantify. You have made the hard calls when someone was not clearing the bar. Currently hands-on. You read and write code, you can take apart a design document or an eval harness and find the flaw in it, and you command distributed systems, service architecture, data-intensive applications, and cloud infrastructure at scale. Experience scaling and modernizing a large existing codebase without stopping the business. You have replaced load-bearing systems in flight, not only built greenfield. Experience leading a globally distributed, remote team at a technology or hyper-growth company is required. A high-volume, two-sided marketplace or multi-tenant platform is a significant plus. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills. Speed, ownership, and quality. You move with urgency, decide without perfect information, and treat everything you deliver as a reflection of yourself. You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do. Essential Job Functions Regularly and reliably attend scheduled virtual team meetings on camera. Work independently with minimal supervision. Use all required digital collaboration tools. Prioritize and self-manage workflows and deadlines. US FLSA Classification: Full-Time/Exempt Compensation Additional Information

  • Stand up the shared AI architecture and evals, and put one agentic workflow into production with a baseline and a measured result.

In the first six months, expect to:

  • Show business impact from agents in production in at least two core workflows, with the evidence behind it.
  • Have the leadership team you need, with the bar visibly raised, and throughput and reliability moving on the paths that matter most.

In the first year, expect to:

  • Run an engineering organization recognized inside and outside Toptal as one of the most advanced in the industry, with the pull on AI now coming from engineering.
  • Have AI leverage embedded in the architecture and the operating model, not living in a portfolio of pilots, and the team you built delivering against plan.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field is required, and an advanced degree is strongly preferred.
  • 15+ years of progressive engineering leadership, including significant time as a CTO or VP of Engineering, or as a direct report to one at meaningful scale.
  • Deep, current, hands-on command of modern AI engineering: foundation models, agentic architectures, harness design, retrieval, context engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation. You have shipped and operated these in production, and you know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up.
  • Agentic systems deployed at scale against real business processes, with measured outcomes on cost, cycle time, quality, or revenue, and a record of retiring what did not work.
  • Rigor about evaluation. You can explain precisely how you knew a model, prompt, or agent change was an improvement, and you can show the evidence.
  • Command of the economics underneath it: model routing, hosted versus self-hosted, inference capacity, latency and cost budgets, and staying portable across providers.
  • Further ahead on AI than the executives around you, able to teach it, and proven at moving an organization to adopt something it was not asking for.
  • You create strategy rather than administer it, and you win arguments on evidence rather than authority, including your view on what a team should look like in the age of AI.
  • Proven ownership of resourcing and workforce planning, and a hiring track record you can quantify. You have made the hard calls when someone was not clearing the bar.
  • Currently hands-on. You read and write code, you can take apart a design document or an eval harness and find the flaw in it, and you command distributed systems, service architecture, data-intensive applications, and cloud infrastructure at scale.
  • Experience scaling and modernizing a large existing codebase without stopping the business. You have replaced load-bearing systems in flight, not only built greenfield.
  • Experience leading a globally distributed, remote team at a technology or hyper-growth company is required. A high-volume, two-sided marketplace or multi-tenant platform is a significant plus.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
  • Speed, ownership, and quality. You move with urgency, decide without perfect information, and treat everything you deliver as a reflection of yourself.
  • You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

Essential Job Functions

  • Regularly and reliably attend scheduled virtual team meetings on camera.
  • Work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Use all required digital collaboration tools.
  • Prioritize and self-manage workflows and deadlines.

SeatGeek believes live events are powerful experiences that unite humans. With our technological savvy and fan-first attitude we’re simplifying and modernizing the ticketing industry.

Reporting to the VP of Engineering, the Director of Engineering will lead the engineering organization responsible for the systems at the core of how teams, venues, and promoters manage tickets and operate their businesses. Hundreds of major live event venues around the globe rely on the SeatGeek platform, including those home to the Dallas Cowboys, Cleveland Cavaliers, Florida Panthers, and Manchester United F.C.

You will set technical direction for this complex, mature platform while helping lead its evolution toward SeatGeek’s next generation of products and architecture. At the same time, you will help change how we build software as we move toward an AI-native engineering organization.

This role requires someone who can move comfortably between technology, product, and the ticketing domain. You will partner closely with Product and Design leadership, Engineering Managers, Senior Engineers, and our clients to turn complicated business problems into clear technical and product direction.

What you'll do

  • Set technical direction across US Ticketing, working with Engineering Managers and Staff+ engineers on architecture, system ownership, modernization, and platform boundaries
  • Lead the evolution of a mature, business-critical platform, balancing client commitments and near-term delivery with long-term reliability, scalability, and modernization
  • Stay close to the technology and contribute directly when useful, whether through code, prototypes, debugging, architecture reviews, technical designs, or documentation
  • Pioneering AI-native engineering by evolving how teams design, build, test, operate, and understand software, and by turning successful experiments into repeatable improvements
  • Partner as a peer with Product and Design leadership to shape strategy, not simply execute a roadmap
  • Develop a deep understanding of our clients and business, distinguish client-specific needs from durable platform opportunities, and participate directly in important client, sales, and implementation conversations when engineering context matters
  • Lead and develop Engineering Managers and senior technical leaders, creating clear ownership and strong leverage through others
  • Build a strong engineering organization by developing leaders, growing Staff+ talent, and evolving team structure as the business changes
  • Create an engineering culture that combines high ownership, healthy technical debate, strong execution, and sustainable performance

What you have

  • Experience leading multiple engineering teams and Engineering Managers in a complex software organization
  • Strong technical judgment and enough architectural depth to work credibly with senior engineers on difficult system and platform decisions
  • A willingness and ability to contribute technically when it is the highest-leverage way to help, including architecture, technical writing, prototyping, debugging, and code
  • Hands-on experience with AI-assisted software development and a strong point of view on how AI changes engineering practices and the software development lifecycle
  • Experience evolving mature, business-critical systems while continuing to deliver customer value
  • A track record of creating technical strategy from ambiguous product and business problems
  • Experience partnering closely with senior Product and Design leaders and learning complex customer domains quickly
  • Experience developing Engineering Managers and Staff+ engineers and creating leverage through other leaders
  • Strong cross-functional leadership, communication, ownership, and comfort making consequential decisions with incomplete information
  • Experience with ticketing, live events, commerce, payments, reservations, inventory, or similarly complex transactional systems is a plus

Our stack

US Ticketing includes mature systems that have powered some of the world’s largest live events for years alongside newer services and applications. We care much more about your ability to understand complex systems, make sound architectural decisions, lead modernization, and use new tools effectively than experience with any particular language or framework.

This is a deeply technical leadership role. We do not expect the Director to be the primary implementer, but we do expect them to be willing and able to contribute technically when it helps move the team forward. AI is becoming a core part of our engineering process, and this leader will help us rethink how teams build and evolve software in an AI-native development environment.

Perks

  • Equity stake
  • Discretionary annual bonus
  • Flexible work environment, allowing you to work as many days a week in the office as you’d like or 100% remotely
  • A WFH stipend to support your home office setup
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Up to 16 weeks of fully-paid family leave
  • 401(k) matching
  • Student loan matching program
  • Health, vision, dental, and life insurance
  • Up to $25k towards family building, reproductive health services and Gender-affirming care
  • $500 per year for wellness expenses
  • Subscriptions to Headspace (meditation), Headspace Care (therapy), and One Medical
  • $360 per quarter to spend on tickets to live events
  • Annual subscription to Spotify, Apple Music, or Amazon music

The salary range for this role is $236,000-$341,000 USD. This role is equity eligible. In addition, you may receive a discretionary annual bonus based on individual and company performance. Phantom has reached #1 in Google Play's finance category and consistently ranks in the top 50 apps across all categories. Phantom partners with many of the most trusted and influential names in finance like Hyperliquid, Stripe, Kalshi and Visa, to make the most popular and innovative financial products accessible to everyone. This is a business-critical area where bugs can lock users out or put funds at risk. You'll ship TypeScript across browser, Node.js, and mobile runtimes (e.g., Hermes) to keep these foundations fast, secure, and reliable. Ship passkeys (WebAuthn) and MFA improvements with a strong security/usability balance. Own onboarding and key lifecycle flows: key generation/derivation, seed phrase flows, seedless registration, hardware wallet pairing. Own sensitive key export/import experiences and related safety rails. Write and maintain high-signal, non-flaky tests (unit/integration/e2e) for critical paths; ensure safe rollouts via monitoring and staged releases. Proven ability to build high-signal, low-flake test suites for critical systems. Familiarity with auth concepts and common mechanisms (sessions/tokens, MFA/OTP, WebAuthn/passkeys) Strong engineering fundamentals: system design, debugging, and production reliability. Nice-to-have Deeper experience with OAuth2/OIDC, WebAuthn internals, cryptography, or key management systems. Web3/wallet or signing-flow experience. Security- or money-adjacent experience (identity, payments, custody). Rust experience (or strong interest in learning it). Our dedication to a secure and seamless user experience has made us the leading wallet on Solana as well as our multi-chain approach enhances our platform's versatility, meeting the needs of a diverse and growing user base. By staying at the forefront of technology and user expectations, we continue to innovate and set industry standards on self-custodial crypto wallets. There has never been a better time to work in crypto to help shape the future of innovation with a focus around the wallet experience! First impressions matter: Wallets are responsible for a users first impression with crypto and onboarding new users into crypto. By ensuring that a user has a great first-time experience with crypto, we can help supercharge the growth of the entire ecosystem. Make crypto easier to navigate: There is no easy way for a user to discover and navigate all that crypto has to offer. Wallets have a unique opportunity to help users not only onboard to crypto but also stay retained by exploring new things to do. We live in a multi-chain world: We currently support Solana, Ethereum, Polygon and Bitcoin with more networks to come in the new future. We are focused on creating a unified, multi-chain crypto experience for users. We believe that our work is stronger with a variety of perspectives, and we’re eager to further diversify our company. If you have a background that you feel would make an impact at Phantom, please consider applying. Who We Are

Our mission is to make the world programmable. Sight is one of the key ways we understand the world, and soon this will be true for the software we use, too.

We’re building the tools, community, and resources needed to make the world programmable with artificial intelligence. Roboflow simplifies building and using computer vision models. Today, over 1M+ developers, including those from half the Fortune 100, use Roboflow’s machine learning open source and hosted tools. Roboflow is supported by great customers and investors, having raised over 63 million from Y Combinator, Google Ventures, Craft Ventures, Sam Altman, Lachy Groom, amongst other leading software investors.

Roboflowers are passionate builders who value ownership, accountability, and a bias toward action. We're curious, hands-on with new tech, and prefer showing our work over talking about it. Many of us have a founder mindset and thrive in our high-autonomy environment.

What You'll Do

You’ll be responsible for driving our goals for enabling every developer to build with computer vision. You’re not starting from scratch, over a million developers use Roboflow today. We have the raw materials ready to be molded and scaled by a DevRel leader.

Responsibilities include:

  • Drive awareness and adoption of Roboflow tools in the developer community

  • Develop tools and integrations to help make Roboflow easier and better for software developers to use

  • Build projects that will help improve the bleeding edge of the main Roboflow product

  • Create demos, applications, and technical content while sharing your progress online and promoting Roboflow on social media (ie X, LinkedIn, Twitch, etc)

  • Create content to educate, inspire, and equip technical audiences with tools and techniques that make them better at their craft

  • Work with Product, Engineering, and Design to develop new projects in support of the launch of new features

  • Write guides, examples, and documentation to make our software more accessible and understandable.

  • Be an active participant in communities like HN, relevant subreddits, Discord groups, GitHub Issues, and the Roboflow forum.

You may also have or quickly develop ideas for amplifying and expanding our community even more -- and we can’t wait to support those as well.

Who You Are

  • 4+ years of engineering experience

  • 2 + years of DevRel related experience, preference for products in B2B, AI, cloud, and/or developer tools

  • Track record of shipping software projects with fast adoption and viral growth, either as part of a previous job or on your own

  • Technical background that enables you to build fast and learn new things quickly

  • Translate complex information into engaging and easy-to-understand content, guides, tutorials, examples, and applications

  • End-to-end content creation skillset across written, video, and social media

  • Self-starter with the ability to analyze ambiguous situations, develop a plan, execute and iterate

  • Operate with urgency, build consensus, and lead cross-functional teams.

  • Customer focus and motivated to become an expert on our industry, customers, product, ecosystem, and competitors.

  • Active contributor to communities online and/or in-person

  • Bonus: you currently have an engaged following online and an interest in growing your personal audience

Who You'll Be Working With

You will directly be working with our Marketing Lead, Open Source Lead, co-founders, Product Engineers, and Product Designers.

We are currently a team of 70 team members located all over the US and Europe. Our team’s backgrounds range from high school whiz kids, former founders of technology companies and fashion lines, world-class engineers, CMOs to CEOs, and have experience scaling businesses to millions in revenue. We want to work with exceptional people with a diverse background. At this early stage, you'll have the ability to work cross-functionally with many members of the team and solve a wide array of problems.

Where You'll Work

Roboflow is distributed across the US and Europe. We currently have Hubs in New York City and San Francisco with a mindset of opening more offices as we grow. We provide opportunities (like team onsites in different cities) and resources (like a travel stipend) to work in person with other team members as much as you'd like, while also supporting remote team members. You can work from one of our Hubs, work from home, work at co-working spaces, etc. We want you to work where you work best. Learn more about how we work at Roboflow.

When You'll Work

We don’t have a particular time-zone preference for this role. We have a flexible schedule that allows you to work collaboratively with other team members and asynchronously when needed.

What You'll Receive

To determine your salary, we use a number of market and data-driven salary sources. We review all salaries every 6 months to ensure we stay in line with the market.

In addition to our cash compensation, we offer generous perks and benefits. Below are some of the highlights:

  • $4000/yr Travel Stipend to travel anywhere anytime to work alongside other Roboflowers

  • $350/mo Productivity stipend to spend on things that make your work environment more productive, like high-speed internet at home or a co-working space

  • $350/mo AI Tools

  • $150/mo Team lunch

  • $500/one time Home office

  • Cover up to 100% of your health insurance costs for you and your partner or family

  • Equity in the company so we are all invested in the future of computer vision

Interview Process

Below is the interview process you can expect for this role. We are all motivated to work with an exceptional team and don't currently have recruiters at Roboflow. You will be speaking directly with our team about what it's like to work and thrive here. We like to work fast at Roboflow, so don't be surprised if all the below conversations happen over a day or two.

Introduction Phase:

[45m] Meet with hiring manager, Trevor Lynn to assess for overall mindset and skill set

Team Interview Phase:

[2 x 60m] Meet with the team

[30m] Meet with hiring manager

Use this time to review specifics about the job description and ask questions before the project phase begins.

Project Phase:

You’ll build a project with Roboflow within a specified amount of time.

We check references and conduct a background check.

Final Interview Stage:

[60m] Meet with Co-founder & CTO

[60m] Meet with CEO

[30m] Meet with Head of Operations to discuss culture

Note: you are welcome to request additional conversations with anyone you would like to meet and we will accommodate as best we can.

Not sure if this is you?

We want a diverse, global team, with a broad range of experience and perspectives. Roboflow is an equal opportunity workplace; we welcome people from all backgrounds, communities, and experiences.

If this job sounds great, but you’re not sure if you qualify, apply to our Former Founders role or subscribe to our career newsletter by emailing "Subscribe" to operations@roboflow.com. We carefully consider every application, and will either move forward with you, find another team that might be a better fit, keep in touch for future opportunities, or thank you for your time.

Equal Employment Opportunity

At Roboflow, we believe great ideas come from everywhere—and everyone. We’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristics.

Roboflow primarily operates during the daytime hours in the US and there are some synchronous meetings you’ll be expected to attend each week. Apart from that, we have a flexible schedule that allows you to work collaboratively with other team members and asynchronously when needed.

What You'll Receive

To determine your salary, we use a number of market and data-driven salary sources. We review all salaries every six months to ensure we stay in line with the market.

The target compensation for this role is $165,000 - $195,000 base.

In addition to our cash compensation, we offer generous perks and benefits. Below are some of the highlights:

  • $4000/yr Travel Stipend to travel anywhere anytime to work alongside other Roboflowers

  • $350/mo Productivity stipend to spend on things that make your work environment more productive, like high-speed internet at home or a co-working space

  • $350/mo AI Tools stipend

  • $150/mo team lunch stipend

  • $500/one time home office stipend

  • Cover up to 100% of your health insurance costs for you and your partner or family

  • Equity in the company so we are all invested in the future of computer vision

Interview Process (6+ hours)

Below is the interview process you can expect for this role. We are all motivated to work with an exceptional team and don't currently have in-house recruiters. You will be speaking directly with our team about what it's like to work and thrive at Roboflow. We like to be decisive and work fast, so don't be surprised if all the below conversations happen over a day or two.

Introduction Phase:

  • [30m] Meet with hiring manager for introduction to assess overall mindset and skillset.

  • [60m] Technical assessment with a Roboflow engineer.

Build with Roboflow Phase:

  • You will build a small project with Roboflow to showcase your technical and product skills.

Team Interview Phase:

  • [45m] Meet with your hiring manager and our CTO to demo your project

Final Interview Stage:

  • [45m] Meet with Head of Operations for a culture discussion.

  • [60m / Optional] Meet with CEO.

Not sure if this is you?

We want a diverse, global team with a broad range of experience and perspectives. If this job sounds great, but you’re not sure if you qualify, look into our Former Founders role or subscribe to our career newsletter by emailing "Subscribe" to operations@roboflow.com. We carefully consider every application and will either move forward with you, find another team that might be a better fit, keep in touch for future opportunities, or thank you for your time.

Equal Employment Opportunity

At Roboflow, we believe great ideas come from everywhere—and everyone. We’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristics.

title: Staff Product Engineer
description: Who we are Help Scout started in 2011 with a simple premise: support software should treat customers like people, not tickets. 3+ billion conversations later, more than 10,000 companies use Help Scout to grow relationships with customers of all types, from clients to patients and beyond. Now we’re in a new chapter: not only building AI that gives teams more space to focus on the customer experience, but also reimagining how we operate in an AI-native world. That means shipping and learning faster, without compromising on craft. Great work here carries a strong opinion and sweats the details, regardless of the tools we use to drive it. We’ve been a fully remote team since day one, with 120+ teammates now all over the world. It’s a culture where you’ll be trusted to take ownership, stay curious, and raise the quality of work around you. It comes with clear expectations and a team that will push you to do some of the best work of your career. If that kind of challenge gives you energy, we’d love to meet you. About this role This role sits on our Agents team — the group building the AI-powered experiences our customers use every day. It's where large language models stop being a demo and become a dependable part of the product: answers, drafts, and assistive features that have to be fast, trustworthy, and genuinely useful in front of real customers. We're looking for an engineer who can build that end-to-end — from the retrieval and agentic plumbing behind a feature to the polished, fast, accessible interface a support agent actually touches. You'll have a frontend center of gravity (strong JavaScript/TypeScript and real front-end craft) while operating as a full-stack product engineer who owns the whole thing. How we work Engineers at Help Scout own their work end-to-end — from problem definition through production, and from the customer signal that shaped the bet to the dashboard that tells you whether it landed. You're full-stack capable, customer-fluent, and genuinely fast with AI tools. You ship the whole thing, not just your layer. We develop in Kotlin, Java, TypeScript, React , and PHP. We leverage Elasticsearch, ClickHouse, Kafka, Flink, RabbitMQ, MySQL, and PostgreSQL — plus vector search and LLM tooling for our AI features. We're heavy users of the AWS ecosystem, Slack, GitHub, and Linear. We use AI tools — Cursor, Claude Code, and a growing set of internal tools — every day. We treat our AI workflow as a product we're shaping together, and we expect you to help shape it. Teams are small and project-based. You might be 3 engineers and a PM on one project, 2 engineers and a designer on the next, or holding more of the product thinking yourself. You're expected to operate well across different compositions and ship end-to-end. What you'll do Ship customer-facing AI features across the full stack. Build the experience and what's behind it — LLM-backed flows, retrieval (RAG) and embeddings, and agentic tool-calling — through to a fast, accessible, well-crafted UI. Most engineers here have a strength; yours leans frontend , and you take initiative across every layer. Treat AI output as something you verify, not assume. Build evaluations, guardrails, and monitoring into AI features so quality is measurable and holds up in production. Know when to trust a model's output and when to push back — and design the system so the product degrades gracefully when a model or provider misbehaves. Sweat the front-end craft. The interface is where AI either earns or loses customer trust. You care about responsiveness, streaming/loading states, accessibility, and the small details that make an assistive feature feel reliable rather than gimmicky. Stay close to customers. Join customer calls when more context is needed to design the right solution, participate in a support escalation rotation, and watch session recordings on the features you own. Bring that signal back into the work. Own outcomes, not just output. Before a project starts, you and a PM agree on a specific outcome metric the work is trying to move. You instrument it, and after it ships you're watching the dashboard and talking to customers — deciding what to do next, not just closing a Linear issue. Co-author the solution. PMs own strategy and sequencing; you bring the judgment and craft for how solutions actually get built, and you'll often shape the product thinking too. The best work happens when engineers, designers, and PMs support each other. Own production readiness from the start. Automation, reliability, monitoring, alerting, and logging aren't afterthoughts — they're part of how you ship. The work continues after merge. Use AI tools every day as part of your craft. We expect fluency with Cursor, Claude Code, or similar. If you saw a way to make the team's AI workflow better tomorrow, you'd say so. Help us hire. From time to time, partner with our Talent team to interview future teammates — one of the highest-leverage things any engineer here does. About you You're a strong, full-stack-capable engineer with a frontend center of gravity. You have substantial JavaScript/TypeScript and React experience and real front-end craft, and you take initiative across the stack and ship end-to-end without waiting for someone to own the other half. You've built real things with LLMs — not just prototypes. You're comfortable with retrieval (RAG), embeddings, prompt/context engineering, and agentic/tool-calling patterns, and you have a point of view on what makes AI features actually reliable in production. You hold a high bar for AI quality. You think in terms of evaluation, verification, and guardrails; you measure whether an AI feature works rather than assuming it does; and you know that more AI-generated code is not the same as more value. You're genuinely fluent with AI coding tools and treat them as part of your craft. You move fast without sacrificing judgment, and you have a point of view on where these tools are heading. You're customer-fluent. You actively seek out customer signal because it's how you stay connected to whether your work is actually solving the problem. You own outcomes. You measure your work by whether it landed — and you're comfortable saying "this didn't move what we hoped, here's what we want to try next," then following through. You take real ownership of the full development lifecycle — automation, reliability, resilience, monitoring, alerting, and logging built in from the start. You stay with what you ship until the metric moves and the customer is better off. You communicate clearly in writing and in conversation. Help Scout is fully remote and writing is the medium of most decisions. You give and receive direct feedback, and you see code review and pairing as real chances to teach and learn. Nice to have Experience making LLM features production-grade: latency/cost tuning, fallbacks and circuit breakers across providers, moderation/safety, and handling sensitive data responsibly. Familiarity with evaluation/observability tooling for AI (LLM-as-judge, test sets, tracing) and the discipline of building representative eval sets. Design sensibility — comfort partnering closely with designers and elevating the craft of an interface, not just implementing a spec. Experience in customer support, productivity, or other tools where trust and reliability are the product. Company values Happy to Help Help is in our first name! We show up for each other — not out of obligation, but because we’re invested in the team’s collective success. We share knowledge freely, lead with generosity, and practice empathy with our teammates, customers, and community. Craft over Convention Our success relies on the quality and craft of the work we put into the world. The status quo simply won’t work. So we insist on narrow focus, sweating every detail, and relentless pursuit of customer delight. Progress not Perfection Achieving our true potential — collectively and individually — requires constant progress and forward momentum. By creating a culture of curiosity and openness, we aim to create a safe space for mistakes, the ability to identify them quickly, and use them to get better. Own the Outcome Own the outcome means taking full responsibility for the results of your work, decisions, and contributions. It reflects a mindset of accountability, proactiveness, and follow-through. If you “own the outcome,” you don’t just complete tasks, you ensure your work leads to meaningful results, and take initiative to solve problems rather than passing them along. Read more about how we define, share, and live these values here . Benefits And Perks Competitive salary and an internal, transparent salary formula based on market data Flexible time off – you choose the holidays and vacations that make sense for you 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave for all new parents, including adoption and foster care A home office stipend to help you get set up and productive A co-working stipend up to $300 a month if you choose to work out of your house A yearly professional development stipend of $1,800 to help you grow in your craft If you’re in the U.S. or Canada, we offer top tier health insurance for you and your dependents. Hiring Guidelines: All roles at Help Scout are fully remote. Some positions have specific location requirements. For roles outside the U.S. and Canada, we work with teammates as independent contractors under country-specific agreements. We do not sponsor visas. Teammates must already be authorized to work from their home country. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a company that embraces and celebrates diversity and inclusion . We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We have read the studies and understand that diverse teams build better products, bring more perspective to the table, contribute to a company’s financial success, and help foster a more inclusive environment for all employees, but the bottom line is that it's the right thing to do. To provide you with the best experience, we can support you with accommodations or adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process. Simply inform our recruitment team during your conversation with them. A note on the use of AI in our interview process While we understand that AI is an important tool in a modern skillset, we ask that you do not utilize AI assistants live on our interviews. Of course, use any tools you need to prepare! But we'd like for you to have a real human-to-human conversation with our team. On our end, we utilize a platform called Brighthire as a notetaker and review tool to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process. Beware of scammers! All legitimate communication from Help Scout regarding your application will come directly from an @ helpscout.com email address and through our applicant tracking system, Ashby. We will never ask for personal financial information or conduct interviews outside of these official channels.

title: Fullstack Engineer
description: About Us The financial advisory industry is a $80T market in the US, but has seen little technological innovation compared to the self-service market (Robinhood, Betterment, Wealthfront, SoFi). Client data management is a universally painful and expensive problem for financial advisors. Today, advisors manually collect, update, and utilize client data across the 7-10 software tools that they use to run their business.
